merlinlib.notice.config_ui: MerlinLib: to keep the code small, the configuration screen was rebuilt for 0.9.0; on Forge and Fabric the visual configuration screen needs Cloth Config API or Jupiter. This notice can be switched off in the configuration file.
merlinlib.configuration.title: MerlinLib configuration (%s)
merlinlib.configuration.title.tooltip: Every MerlinLib switch is a NeoForge configuration option: this screen is built from the mod's specification, and the file it edits is in config/.
merlinlib.configuration.section.merlinli: merlinlib-client.toml - this computer only: display, particles, the editor and macros.
merlinlib-client.toml - this computer only: display, particles, the editor and macros.
merlinlib-common.toml - authoritative for the game: permissions, the toolkit limits and the join notices.
merlinlib-common.toml - authoritative for the game: permissions, the toolkit limits and the join notices.
merlinlib.configuration.client.general.t: Settings that belong to the file as a whole.
merlinlib.configuration.client.general.c: Written by the mod, read only to bring a file from an older build up to the current layout. Do not set it back by hand.
merlinlib.configuration.client.general.n: The chat notice that says the configuration screen was rebuilt. Business mods' notices are switched in the [notices] section of the common file, not here.
merlinlib.configuration.client.hud.cross: Show the damage of the weapon you just used near the crosshair. This is the weapon's listed damage, not the health actually removed.
How long the number stays on screen, in ticks. 20 ticks = 1 second.
merlinlib.configuration.client.hud.colla: Fold a very large health bar into one heart plus the exact numbers, instead of drawing one heart per two points. Up to the threshold below the bar stays plain vanilla.
Health above which the bar folds.
merlinlib.configuration.client.hud.armou: Move the armour bar up against the folded health row.
merlinlib.configuration.client.floating_: Damage numbers flying off a mob when it is hit.
Show damage numbers flying off a mob when it is hit. Off by default: it is a testing aid, so it is something a player turns on.
How long a damage number stays visible after a mob is hit, in ticks.
Base scale of a damage number. Higher means larger text.
ARGB colour of a normal hit, written as 0xRRGGBB (or 0xAARRGGBB), #RRGGBB or a palette name.
ARGB colour of a critical hit, in the same forms.
Upper bound on simultaneous damage numbers; the oldest one is dropped first.
merlinlib.configuration.client.particles: Limits on the particles this client draws.

Some paths of the game ask for one particle per point of damage, so a single hit with a very large number can freeze the client. When enabled, at most the limit below are drawn per 1/20 second; the rest are dropped before they exist.
512 is far above what normal play produces (rain, explosions, a busy farm) and still keeps a damage number in the thousands from freezing the client. Lower it if a very large hit still stutters.
merlinlib.configuration.client.editor.ho: Off by default, so the library can be installed without claiming a key. Toggle it in game with /merlinlib editorhotkey on.
merlinlib.configuration.client.editor.sh: Value change when a - or + button is clicked while holding shift.
merlinlib.configuration.client.editor.sc: Value change per mouse wheel notch over a number field.
Value change per mouse wheel notch while holding ctrl.
merlinlib.configuration.client.macros.en: Enable the macro screen and running macros from their bound keys.
merlinlib.configuration.common.general.t: Settings that belong to the file as a whole.
merlinlib.configuration.common.general.c: Written by the mod, read only to bring a file from an older build up to the current layout. Leave it alone; setting it back only repeats the migration.
Who may use the testing toolkit.
When true, only operators may use the testing toolkit: the editors, the health editor and the macros.
Require operator permission to open the item editor.
Require operator permission to open the health editor.
merlinlib.configuration.common.tools.too: The testing toolkit and its limits.
merlinlib.configuration.common.tools.ena: Master switch of the testing screens: with it off, no toolkit screen opens. The testing items stay in the creative tab.
merlinlib.configuration.common.tools.max: Upper bound for the damage value of the test weapons. Defaults to the integer limit.
Upper bound for enchantment levels set through the item editor. Defaults to the integer limit.
merlinlib.configuration.common.tools.all: Allow levels above the enchantment's own maximum
When true, an enchantment may be raised above the maximum level its own definition declares. On by default: the ceiling that matters is the level limit above.
Allow enchantments the item cannot carry
When true, any enchantment may be added to any item, for example efficiency on a sword. Off by default: an enchantment the item cannot normally carry has no effect in game.
When true, the item editor opens for every item, including blocks and other things that are not weapons, tools or equipment. Off by default.
When true, the base damage of an ordinary weapon can be edited too, not only of a testing weapon. Off by default: ordinary weapons are what vanilla balance and other mods rely on.
merlinlib.configuration.common.tools.hea: The health editor requires the item
When true, the health editor only opens while holding the health editor item.
merlinlib.configuration.common.content.d: Emergency switch: when true, none of the enchantments defined in config/MerlinLib/*.json are generated. Code api registrations are unaffected.
merlinlib.configuration.common.notices.t: Join notices, offered to every player who joins.
merlinlib.configuration.common.notices.e: Show the join notices business mods registered through MerlinLib. Takes effect on the next join.
merlinlib.configuration.common.notices.p: Written as "<modid>=true;<modid>=false>". A mod that is not listed uses the default it declared when it registered. Editing this line by hand works too.
